title: Integral inverse image preserves $\Dbc$ and agrees with the completed inverse image
statement:
Let $g\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of standing schemes and
$g^*\colon\D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)\to\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$ the inverse image.

1. $g^*$ maps $\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ into $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$.
2. For $K\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ the natural map
   $$
   c_K\colon g^*K\longrightarrow R\varprojlim_ng^{-1}\bigl(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n\bigr)
   $$
   is an isomorphism. After restriction of scalars to the constant sheaf
   $\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ the target is the completed inverse image of
   the Stacks Project (Stacks, Tags 099I, 099N), so on
   $\Dbc(-,\mathcal O_E)$ the inverse image $g^*$ agrees with the completed inverse
   image.

proof.text: Cartesian coefficients identify $g^*$ with exact inverse image. Applying it to kernels and images gives $H^q(g^*N)=g^*H^q(N)$; it preserves bounds and mapping-cone triangles. The finite-model pullback lemma preserves constructible cohomology, using the same scalar presentations on base-changed strata and covers.

source.place: First paragraph and Local models; old steps 1--2

proof.text: For a stratum generator $a_!M$ of the shriek lemma, the base-changed covering carries the same bounded finite free scalar complex: exact pullback and the coefficient isomorphisms preserve its terms and scalar differentials. Step 1 gives bounded constructible cohomology for $g_S^*M$. The bounded stratum base-change lemma identifies $g^*a_!M$ with $a'_!g_S^*M$, which is bounded constructible by clause (1) of the shriek lemma.

The objects $N$ with $g^*N$ bounded constructible form a full subcategory closed under isomorphisms and two-out-of-three on triangles: step 1 preserves triangles and the integral-heart lemma makes $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ triangulated. Step 2 supplies all generators. Clause (2) of the shriek lemma therefore proves (1) by finite-stratum dévissage.

By (1), proved in step 3, $g^*K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Clause (2) of the integral-model criterion on $Y$ and $X$ makes $K$ and $g^*K$ derived complete; its hypotheses are exactly the standing separated finite-type characteristic-$p$ setting, with $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite and $\ell\ne p$. Let $P$ be the flat-term K-flat representative of $K$ with which the completed-pullback definition defines $c_K$; then $c_K$ is the localization of $\alpha_T$ for the strict tower $T_n=g^*(P\otimes_{R_Y}A_{n,Y})$. The first chain equality $L_P\alpha_T=\alpha_U$ of the strict Roos normalization lemma identifies $c_K$, including transitions and augmentation, with the completion unit of $g^*K$, computed on the flat-term K-flat representative $g^*P$. That unit is invertible by the definition of derived completeness, proving the first assertion of (2).

source.place: First paragraph and Local models; old steps 7--8

proof.text: Use the second normalized equality of the strict Roos lemma: the restriction of $c_K$ is the constant-coefficient quotient-tower unit, with source identification $d$ and target identification $E_P$. Clause (2) of the integral-model criterion places $\operatorname{Res}_YK$ in the constant derived-complete constructible category. The completed-pullback definition identifies precisely this tower and unit with Stacks completed inverse image (099N(2),(5)). This proves the scalar-restriction assertion of (2).
